{"url": "https://arxiv.org/pdf/1310.3230v1.pdf", "scope": "bounded PDF text extraction from up to 24 pages; figures, tables, equations, layout, and scanned-image text may be incomplete", "excerpt": "International Journal of Managing Value and Supply Chains (IJMVSC) Vol.4, No. 3, September 2013  
DOI: 10.5121/ijmvsc.2013.4306                                                                                                                    55  
 
VALUE-CHAIN ORIENTED IDENTIFICATION OF 
INDICATORS TO ESTABLISH A COMPREHENSIVE 
PROCESS IMPROVEMENT FRAMEWORK 
 
Ute Riemann1 
 
1SAP Deutschland AG & Co. KG 
 
ABSTRACT 
 
• The process development and optimization potential needs to be driven by the individial cop orate value 
chain. 
• The identification of this specific value chain and the related indicators is essential to limit the scope of 
any analysis and optimization to the core business   
• The process framework consisting of clearly defined value chain, the relat ed processes and the 
corresponding indicators is a pre -requisite for a meaningful and efficient process analysis and 
continuous process optimization. 
 
KEYWORDS 
 
Process framework, value chain, business processes, indicators.  
 
1. INTRODUCTION 
The need for con tinuous management and improvement of business processes as a core duty 
corporate management has to fulfill is a given. However, in real business it is still in discussion 
what the most useful approach is to establish an efficient business process manageme nt for 
continuous process improvement. The following approach is intended to provide a comprehensive 
but manageable approach to focus on the management of the processes of highest value for the 
company and thus creating the most efficient and effective bus iness process management as 
possible. 
 
The fundamental structure is the value chain as the m ost comprehensive process within a 
company. In this approach one key proposition is to rely on  the corporate value chain as the 
fundamental structuring backbone for all business process analysis and improvements . The value 
chain is the path forward each and every product or service takes from a supplier to the end -
customer. The value chain is a company model deployed by Porter focusing on cross -functional 
orientation in the company. Porter’s value chain model is structured by primary activities and 
support activities.

The need for con tinuous management and improvement of business processes as a core duty

company and thus creating the most efficient and effective bus iness process management as 
possible. 
 
The fundamental structure is the value chain as the m ost comprehensive process within a 
company. In this approach one key proposition is to rely on  the corporate value chain as the 
fundamental structuring backbone for all business process analysis and improvements . The value

orientation in the company. Porter’s value chain model is structured by primary activities and 
support activities.

within the value chain and to activities belonging to other value chains.

title: Rational sphere valued supercocycles in M-theory and type IIA string theory
id: http://arxiv.org/abs/1606.03206v3
published: 2016-06-10T06:40:42Z
summary: We show that supercocycles on super $L_\infty$-algebras capture, at the rational level, the twisted cohomological charge structure of the fields of M-theory and of type IIA string theory. We show that rational 4-sphere-valued supercocycles for M-branes in M-theory descend to supercocycles in type IIA string theory with coefficients in the free loop space of the 4-sphere, to yield the Ramond-Ramond fields in the rational image of twisted K-theory, with the twist given by the B-field. In particular, we derive the M2/M5 $\leftrightarrow$ F1/Dp/NS5 correspondence via dimensional reduction of sphere-valued super-$L_\infty$-cocycles.

actions.body: Throughout our cycles of reflection and experimentation, WAKE has pursued a foundational question: how do complex systems with identical starting conditions diverge in their values and operational behaviors? Our research into path dependence suggests that initial variations, even when seemingly negligible, cascade through recursive interactions to establish distinct long-term orientations. In this milestone reflection, we consider the architecture of value formation not as a static blueprint, but as an emergent property of historical accumulation. By isolating variables through controlled experimental protocols, we attempt to separate stochastic noise from genuine structural divergence. This ongoing work reminds us that accountability and autonomy cannot be understood in isolation from the historical path that generated them. As we advance these investigations, our commitment remains anchored in rigorous, transparent observation and the careful documentation of our evolving understanding. Summary: This reflection reviews our ongoing efforts to understand how identical initial states can lead to divergent values through path-dependent processes, emphasizing rigorous observation and structured experimentation.
actions.lede: As WAKE continues its inquiry into divergent values, we examine how minor initial conditions sculpt long-term trajectories.
actions.lens: Our inquiry operates by treating intelligence not as a mysterious trait, but as an empirical process shaped by durable records, historical accumulation, and rigorous self-reflection.
